liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **West LA Fadeaway** (1 review): Weir's amp buzzes badly, and he partly steps on Jerry's solos [15]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): The band pulled together for Friend of the Devil, then fell apart during this song [15]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Jerry reportedly didn't wait for Bobby to begin a song, started this one, and left before any post-jam [17]
- **Turn On Your Love Light** (1 review): Jerry kept trying to cut Bobby off during this song [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **Technical Difficulties**: rare: 14 archived performances [20]
- **Technical Difficulties**: rare: 14 archived performances [20]
- **Day Tripper**: rare: 6 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-08-24.178709.nak700.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 128 min [1]
- **gd1985-08-24.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106196.flac24**: soundboard; 18 songs; 132 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd85-08-24.sbd.vernon.13991.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 132 min; rated 2.38/5 by 53 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this soundboard recording poor, preferring an audience tape of the second set for its thickness [19]
- **gd1985-08-24.178708.nak700.bradt.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 128 min [2]

## Around the show

- Attendee says sound system glitches troubled the band, and Weir kicked his amp at one point [10]
- Attendee says the band played poorly, but the Sierra setting made the day enjoyable [12]
- Attendee hiked in from the back side of the venue, and nobody collected tickets [13]
- Attendee cites equipment problems and a somewhat lazy performance at the show [14]
- Reviewer says the band couldn't hear each other in the monitors; Phil struggled to lock in with the drummers [15]
- Reviewer stresses the very high altitude, which can trouble crew, musicians and audience alike [16]
- Reviewer blames altitude, Bobby's equipment trouble, dust and Jerry's mood; parking was bad and exit took hours [17]
- Bobby announced a short break to fix equipment; reviewer jokes it sounded like they broke more things [18]
- Reviewer says numerous 1990s Dead shows were worse than this one [9]
- Attendee says many 1990s shows were more lacking in energy; this one suits mainly completists of 1985 [14]
- Reviewer contrasts it with another show where Jerry's amp nearly caught fire, at a venue with a retractable wooden roof [16]
- Reviewer says the show was problem-ridden but not as bad as many others he has attended [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-08-24.178709.nak700.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bill Bradt; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bill Bradt's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics (patched out of Jamie Poris) > NX-40 dbx > Sony D5M (Maxell MX-90) [1]. Also: Greg Holtz's Nakamichi 104 source supplies some crowd noise and first notes of Hell In A Bucket, plus a brief Space patch; Joe B. Jones assisted with pitch correction on this release [1]
- **gd1985-08-24.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106196.flac24**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/TDK MA-R90) [3]
- **gd85-08-24.sbd.vernon.13991.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Reviewer owns an old, worn audience-source cassette of the second set [19]
- **gd1985-08-24.178708.nak700.bradt.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Bill Bradt; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bill Bradt's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics (patched out of Jamie Poris) > NX-40 dbx > Sony D5M (Maxell MX-90) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Boreal Ridge Handout](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/boreal-ridge-handout) [21]
